color.$description: Semantic colors: what each color is for. They alias the color ramps, which the palette generator solves for each theme, so one file serves the four themes (decisions/0012).

canvas.$description: The ground of a screen, a list or a table.

dev.westron.usage.avoid: Cards and sheets: use background.surface.

surface.$description: Something raised off the canvas: a card, a sheet or a popover westron draws, a dragged row. White in light; one step lighter than the canvas in dark, where higher is lighter.

dev.westron.usage.avoid: A well below the content: use background.sunken.

sunken.$description: A well below the canvas: a sidebar, a code block, a log, a table header.

dev.westron.usage.avoid: A control's fill: use background.muted.

muted.$description: A quiet fill inside content: the track of a segmented control, a tag or a badge without a color, a secondary button, a framed text field. It stands about 1.1:1 off the canvas, so a control found by it alone misses 3:1 for its edge, as the owner accepted for the text field (design-language/08); in high contrast such a control also draws border.strong, or status.danger.border on a destructive secondary button.

dev.westron.usage.avoid: A row under the pointer: use background.hover.

hover.$description: A row or a control under the pointer.

pressed.$description: A row or a control while it is pressed.

muted-hover.$description: The muted fill of a control filled with it and labelled in text.primary, such as a secondary button, under the pointer: background.muted one hover step towards its words (decisions/0012, 0013).

dev.westron.usage.avoid: A fill under colored words, such as a destructive secondary button: use background.muted-hover-colored. A row or an unfilled control under the pointer: use background.hover.

muted-pressed.$description: The muted fill of a control filled with it and labelled in text.primary, such as a secondary button, while it is pressed: background.muted two hover steps towards its words, as far as text.primary still reads on it (decisions/0012, 0013).

dev.westron.usage.avoid: A fill under colored words, such as a destructive secondary button: use background.muted-pressed-colored. A pressed row or an unfilled control: use background.pressed.

muted-hover-colored.$description: The muted fill of a control filled with it and labelled in colored words, such as a destructive secondary button, under the pointer: halfway between background.muted and muted-pressed-colored.

use: destructive secondary button under the pointer
dev.westron.usage.avoid: A fill under text.primary: use background.muted-hover, which moves further towards its words.

muted-pressed-colored.$description: The muted fill of a control filled with it and labelled in colored words, such as a destructive secondary button, while it is pressed: background.muted moved towards its words as far as every colored word, step 11 of every ramp, still reads on it, which is about step 5's tone (decisions/0012, 0013).

dev.westron.usage.avoid: A fill under text.primary: use background.muted-pressed, which moves further towards its words.

selected.$description: A selected row or item, tinted with the accent.

dev.westron.usage.avoid: Color alone: a selected row also shows a mark that is not a color, in every theme, such as a check or ListRow's border.focus bar at its leading edge.

accent-subtle.$description: A quiet accent ground: the tile behind an empty state's icon, a highlighted tip.

accent.$description: The fill of the one primary action on a screen, a checked box, a switch that is on.

dev.westron.usage.avoid: Large areas, and more than one filled control on a screen. Status: use status.info.fill, even though info is the accent's blue today.

accent-hover.$description: The accent fill under the pointer.

accent-pressed.$description: The accent fill while it is pressed: one step beyond accent-hover, further from its label, so text.on-accent reads on it as on the resting fill.

dev.westron.usage.avoid: A resting or hovered fill: use background.accent or background.accent-hover. A pressed row or a quiet control: use background.pressed.

secondary.$description: Text and glyphs that come second: captions, metadata, a row's details, timestamps. On background.muted-hover and muted-pressed it is only a glyph, never text: the icon of an unlit chip under the pointer or pressed, decorative beside the chip's label (spec/components/chip, decisions/0001), so those pairs are non-text, 3:1.

placeholder.$description: The placeholder of an empty field. It meets the text target, as all words do.

on-accent.$description: Text and glyphs on the accent fill, also under the pointer and pressed: white, and the canvas's color in dark high contrast, where the fill turns light.

dev.westron.usage.avoid: Status text: use status.<name>.text.

tertiary.$description: Glyphs that carry no words and need only 3:1: a chevron, a grip, a disclosure triangle.

dev.westron.usage.avoid: Words: words are text.secondary at least.

default.$description: Separators and the outline of a card: decorative in standard themes, 3:1 in high contrast, where every raised surface gets one. In the standard themes also the quiet ring of an unchecked check, below 3:1 by the deviation design-language/08 records; in high contrast that ring is border.strong.

guide.$description: The guides down the levels of a tree, one under each ancestor level of a nested row: decorative in the standard themes, where the indent also shows the nesting, and 3:1 in high contrast on every ground a row stands on, its highlights included, which border.default does not reach there. The palette's guides step (decisions/0012).

strong.$description: The border of a control that must be seen: a radio ring; and in the high-contrast themes a framed text field and a secondary button, where their muted fill alone does not mark their edge against the ground, and an unchecked check's ring, which is border.default in the standard themes. The ground is what that border is measured on, not the fill inside it.

focus.$description: The focus ring, and the bar or outline that marks a selected item, such as a selected ListRow's bar.

insertion.$description: The line that marks where a dragged item would be dropped: an insertion rule; and the ring of a row a dragged item would be dropped onto, on its accent-subtle highlight. The focus ring's blue, a token of its own so that each can change without the other.

danger.$description: The status danger. Something failed or will destroy data: an error, a failed build, a destructive action. A status always comes with an icon and a word, never color alone.

background.$description: The quiet ground of a badge, a banner or a row in the status danger.

border.$description: The border of a field or a banner in the status danger, and of a destructive secondary button in the high-contrast themes.

icon.$description: The icon or dot of the status danger.

fill.$description: The solid fill of the status danger: a button or a count badge.

fill-hover.$description: The danger fill under the pointer: a destructive filled button that is hovered.

dev.westron.usage.avoid: A resting fill or a count badge: use status.danger.fill.

fill-pressed.$description: The danger fill while it is pressed: one step beyond fill-hover, further from its label, so on-fill reads on it as on the resting fill.

dev.westron.usage.avoid: A resting fill or a count badge: use status.danger.fill.

on-fill.$description: Text and glyphs on the danger fill, also under the pointer and pressed.

warning.$description: The status warning. Something needs attention but works: a slow job, a quota near its limit. A status always comes with an icon and a word, never color alone.

background.$description: The quiet ground of a badge, a banner or a row in the status warning.

border.$description: The border of a field or a banner in the status warning.

icon.$description: The icon or dot of the status warning.

fill.$description: The solid fill of the status warning: a button or a count badge.

on-fill.$description: Text and glyphs on the warning fill.

success.$description: The status success. Something finished well: a passed build, a saved change. Bluish green, so that it stays apart from danger for people with color blindness. A status always comes with an icon and a word, never color alone.

background.$description: The quiet ground of a badge, a banner or a row in the status success.

border.$description: The border of a field or a banner in the status success.

icon.$description: The icon or dot of the status success.

fill.$description: The solid fill of the status success: a button or a count badge.

on-fill.$description: Text and glyphs on the success fill.

info.$description: The status info. Neutral news and work in progress: a running job, a tip. It shares the accent's blue. A status always comes with an icon and a word, never color alone.

background.$description: The quiet ground of a badge, a banner or a row in the status info.

border.$description: The border of a field or a banner in the status info.

icon.$description: The icon or dot of the status info.

fill.$description: The solid fill of the status info: a button or a count badge.

on-fill.$description: Text and glyphs on the info fill.

neutral.$description: The status neutral. No verdict: queued, skipped, cancelled, unknown. A status always comes with an icon and a word, never color alone.

background.$description: The quiet ground of a badge, a banner or a row in the status neutral.

border.$description: The border of a field or a banner in the status neutral.

icon.$description: The icon or dot of the status neutral.

fill.$description: The solid fill of the status neutral: a button or a count badge.

on-fill.$description: Text and glyphs on the neutral fill.

category.$description: The list colors: twelve named identity colors for lists, projects and tags. A list color names a thing; it never means a status.

background.$description: The quiet ground of a tag or a row in the list color blue.

border.$description: The border of an outlined tag in the list color blue.

icon.$description: A dot or an icon in the list color blue.

text.$description: Text in the list color blue.

fill.$description: The solid fill of a lit tag in the list color blue.

on-fill.$description: Text and glyphs on the fill of the list color blue.

control.$description: The fill of a checked control in the list color blue, such as the task check: the solid fill, darkened or lightened where it would not stand out from the ground the control sits on (decisions/0012, revision of 2026-11-18).

use: checked control in a list color
dev.westron.usage.avoid: Tags, tiles and statuses: they keep fill, which is not held to the non-text contrast on the ground.

on-control.$description: The mark and any glyph on the control fill of the list color blue.

use: check mark on a checked task check
dev.westron.usage.avoid: Text on a lit tag: use on-fill.

chart.$description: The chart series, in order: the first ones differ most, also for people with color blindness. Each has 3:1 on every ground in every theme; high contrast adds labels and markers, not contrast. More than eight series need direct labels.
